test_tags.title: credit_day=31 is accepted after the CHECK migration and rejected before it

implementation_order.rationale: FIRST: the shipped bonds CHECK (src/db.py: credit_day >= 1 AND credit_day <= 28) must migrate to 1..31 before any D42 form can write a 31st credit day (F-233 seam; D41 owner rule carried into the D42 round). The migration is a table rebuild that preserves every existing row and re-applies the widened CHECK; it has zero code or UI dependencies, so it sits at position 1, and every later insert path (payout editor rows, attribute forms, the move panel's credit-day field) runs against the widened bound instead of tripping the legacy 28 cap. Order rationale: pure schema foundation first, smallest blast radius before any route or template churn. Gate: TC-136 (REMOTE) — before/after acceptance in one case: legacy CHECK rejects credit_day=31 with 400 and zero writes, migrated schema accepts 31, keeps 0/32 rejected, and no row is lost.

implementation_order.entry: Sort-key unification — one shared D43 ordering key

test_tags.title: Dashboard, holdings, payouts, exports and print all emit Danger -> On-going -> Matured order (D43 — table of surfaces)

implementation_order.rationale: SECOND: extract ONE shared sort key — engine HEALTH_ORDER {Danger: 0, On-going: 1, Matured: 2, Invalid: 3} (src/engine.py, sort_payout_rows), Invalid last — and route every list surface through it at the query or model layer; the D43 LOCKED standard forbids per-template or per-screen sorting, so no surface may reimplement the order. The key is a pure read-layer function with no route dependencies, but it must land BEFORE its consumers: the payouts rows (step 3), the dashboard rows (step 5) and the exports/print re-renders exercised by the later steps all read it, so 2 < 3 and 2 < 5. It follows step 1 only per the brief's sequence — schema first, then the shared read-layer key — with no back-edge into step 1. D43 taxonomy and the automatic same-day Danger rule feed the key through read-time derive; display labels never reorder anything. Gate: TC-131 (REMOTE) — the five-surface table (dashboard | holdings | payouts | exports | print) all emit the D43 order and agree with each other.

implementation_order.entry: Payout editor routes + newest-first month headers

test_tags.title: Payout cell edit saves through the existing payment route and status re-derives immediately
Payouts month headers are newest-first and never exceed the current month

implementation_order.rationale: THIRD: the editable payout cell maps onto the EXISTING POST /payment/<bond_id>/<month> route (payment_edit in src/app.py) writing payment_ledger — the F-233 seam rules out a second writer, so the editor is a thin UI over the route plus immediate read-time status re-derivation; the month header set becomes elapsed + current only, newest-left (D42; the F-231 future-column lesson). Depends on step 2: payout rows render through the shared D43 key (Danger top, On-going next, Matured moves down automatically) and on step 1 indirectly (rows saved during e2e carry migrated credit days). Intra-entry: route save and header rule land together as one payouts-surface slice. Gates: TC-129 (save + re-derive + single-writer ledger) and TC-130 (header order and future-month exclusion), both REMOTE.

implementation_order.entry: Attribute ALTER + forms + strips (+ inline move panel)

test_tags.title: Attribute parity roundtrip: candidate -> move -> holdings strip values are equal
Move inline panel renders the exact FR-67..74-bound field labels below the row

implementation_order.rationale: FOURTH: the bonds ALTER adds the missing D42 attribute columns (rating agency, issuer type, secured, face value, payout cycle — the FR-40 display set plus broker and invested/source-note fields), Add Candidate collects them, and the Watchlist Details facts grid and the My Holdings attribute strip display the identical values (D42 attribute parity). The Move inline expansion panel ships in this step too: it carries the credit-day and broker fields the ALTER backs, and its exact field labels are gated here (FR-74). Depends on step 1: both passes rebuild the same bonds table, so the CHECK migration completes first and the attribute ALTER runs second — one migration train, two ordered passes (1 < 4), never two conflicting rebuilds. Gates: TC-133 (candidate -> move -> strip values equal, all seven attributes) and TC-137 (byte-exact labels below the row), both REMOTE.

test_tags.title: Dashboard status filter chips All/Danger/On-going/Matured filter rows with exactly one active chip

implementation_order.rationale: FIFTH: the Dashboard gains its Overview / Returns history tab container and the four status filter chips (All, Danger, On-going, Matured) that narrow the chart rows while the visible set keeps the D43 priority order (D42 dashboard chips + filter; subset of D43). Depends on step 2 (the filtered set still sorts through the shared key) -> 2 < 5; the Returns history tab container it creates is the vessel step 7 populates -> 5 < 7. The FR-73 reference here is the tab shell only — its aggregation lands at step 7. Gate: TC-132 (REMOTE) — exact chip labels, one-active-at-a-time, per-status row counts, All restores everything.

test_tags.title: Email presets autofill exact SMTP values and the test-email route renders success and failure banner states

implementation_order.rationale: SIXTH: Settings > Email ships the provider presets — Gmail autofills smtp.gmail.com / 587 / TLS, Outlook / Microsoft 365 autofills smtp.office365.com / 587 / STARTTLS, Custom clears the three fields — plus the setup guide and a Send test email action backed by a NEW route that persists non-secret config/status through the existing alert_prefs key/value table and sends through mailer.py (F-233 seam: NEW route + alert_prefs persistence; D42 email presets, App-Password-only research). No dependency on steps 1-5 (Settings chrome, alert_prefs and mailer are untouched by them) — placed at position 6 per the brief's sequence so the Settings surface it renders on is final, and it introduces no back-edge. Gate: TC-134 (REMOTE) — exact autofill values, success and failure banner states, alert_prefs persistence, no credential leakage.

test_tags.title: Returns tab computes paid-dot-pending and cumulative running total and the Goals KPI link navigates to it

implementation_order.rationale: SEVENTH: the returns history aggregates payment_ledger GROUP BY month — interest received, positions paid-dot-pending of the active set, cumulative running total, newest-first with the current month highlighted — into the step-5 Returns history tab, and the Financial Goals KPI cards link to it with the view-switch + tab-activation handler (F-233 seam: the #returns link needs view+tab JS; D42 returns history). Depends on step 5 (the tab container exists to receive the panel) -> 5 < 7, and on step 3 (the editor route keeps writing the ledger rows the aggregation reads) -> 3 < 7. Gate: TC-135 (REMOTE) — per-month math, cumulative running total equal to the Received card, newest-first/current-highlight rules, and the Goals link performing both the view switch and the Returns tab activation.

test_tags.title: Full GitHub Actions suite green — every D42/D43 gate plus all pre-existing TCs pass on the merged branch (aggregate gate, not a new TC id)

implementation_order.rationale: LAST: the terminal gate is the GitHub Actions full suite running green — owner Q3 makes testing remote-only, so there is no local pytest tier and CI is the single merge gate. Every step 1-7 change lands behind its own TC (TC-136, TC-131, TC-129, TC-130, TC-133, TC-137, TC-132, TC-134, TC-135), and this step asserts the whole suite — new D42/D43 cases plus every pre-existing TC — passes together on the merged branch. Depends on {1..7}: all earlier steps < 8, no step may merge past a red gate, and a red run sends the failure back to the owning step rather than forward. The tag names the aggregate range TC-129..TC-137 deliberately — step 8 adds no new TC id of its own.
